title: Domain Adaptation and Annotation Efficiency in Remote-Sensing LULC Mapping: A Systematic Review of Active Learning and Vision–Language Models and a Conceptual Framework for the Brazilian Cerrado
content: Accurate and transferable land-use and land-cover (LULC) mapping in the Brazilian Cerrado is challenged by spatial and temporal heterogeneity, domain shift, and the high cost of expert annotation. This systematic review with qualitative methodological synthesizes evidence on Active Learning (AL), domain adaptation, remote-sensing foundation models, and Remote-Sensing Vision–Language Models (RS-VLMs), focusing on their complementary roles in annotation-efficient and transferable LULC mapping. Evidence was synthesized qualitatively because the reviewed studies differed substantially in sensors, tasks, datasets, domain-shift conditions, and evaluation protocols. The literature indicates that uncertainty-, diversity-, and representativeness-based AL can improve annotation efficiency, while foundation models and RS-VLMs provide increasingly transferable representations and few-shot or open-vocabulary capabilities across remote-sensing applications. However, direct empirical evidence integrating transferable representations, AL, and domain adaptation for Cerrado LULC monitoring remains limited. Based on the convergence of these evidence streams, we propose a conceptual human-in-the-loop framework that combines transferable representations with selective target-domain annotation and subsequent adaptation. The framework is hypothesis-driven rather than experimentally validated. The review identifies priorities for empirical evaluation, including multimodal benchmarks, standardized AL protocols, spatially and temporally independent validation, explainability, and continuous human-in-the-loop adaptation. This synthesis provides a methodological basis for future domain-adaptive LULC monitoring in the Brazilian Cerrado.
